links.outcome: Diet plan energy content and expert accuracy scores compared across Turkish and English prompts
links.effect: Energy differed significantly across models and languages (Gemini-English 859.11 ± 151.35 kcal vs Copilot-English 1496.03 ± 249.71 kcal; p < 0.001). Expert accuracy median was 0.00 for ChatGPT-Turkish vs 4.00 for Gemini-English.
links.quote: Significant differences were observed in energy content across models and languages (lowest: Gemini-English: 859.11 ± 151.35 kcal vs. highest: Copilot-English:1496.03 ± 249.71 kcal; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Adherence of LLM-generated renal diets to TUBER 2022 and KDOQI guideline nutrient targets
links.effect: All models' energy fell below reference targets, some potassium outputs exceeded safe limits, and none of the models fully met the guideline requirements.
links.quote: None of the models fully met the guideline requirements.

links.outcome: Suitability of standalone LLM dietary planning for kidney disease patients
links.effect: LLM diets were inconsistent in nutrient accuracy, guideline adherence, and personalization; authors conclude standalone clinical use is inappropriate and expert supervision is required.
links.quote: Their standalone use in clinical practice is therefore not appropriate; expert supervision and integration with clinical guidelines are required.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates outputs (dietary plans) generated by several commercial LLMs against clinical guidelines and expert evaluation using standardized patient scenarios, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
